column2: This is AquaSentinel, live. Our autonomous boat is surveying the lake and streaming pH, oxygen, temperature, conductivity, nitrate and turbidity every second.
Missions are given in plain language, even by voice.
Gemini's planner agent turns it into GPS waypoints, checks every leg stays on water, and re-routes the boat.
This lake is simulated, so I'll plant a hidden industrial discharge that began twelve hours ago. The agents are told nothing.

The detector flags pH, conductivity and temperature off their baseline. Gemini decides to chase it: the boat leaves its route, climbs the pollution gradient, then follows the shoreline until the signal peaks, and marks its source estimate.

The diagnostician fuses sensor readings, the camera frame and CPCB criteria. Likely cause: industrial discharge, with evidence, what doesn't fit, recommended actions and confirming lab tests. And the simulator's hidden source? Right where the boat said.
Our LightGBM fish-health model scores every zone. The south-west is now stressed, and its SHAP factors show exactly why.
Switch the whole interface to Tamil or Hindi. Officials can question the lake by voice, in their own language.
The answer comes back in Tamil, grounded in live data, with every tool call shown.
One click writes community alerts in English, Tamil and Hindi. Another builds a regulator-ready PDF: data tables straight from storage, plus Gemini's narrative.
And every claim is measured against the simulator's hidden truth: source-location error in metres, detection precision and recall, and end-to-end latency.
It runs on phones and tablets, in every language. AquaSentinel: it doesn't just measure water quality, it explains it, and acts on it.
